candidates.attacker_control: The attacker fully controls the HTTP Cookie header, specifically the JSPWikiUID value, on any request (e.g., GET /Logout.jsp or any *.jsp request). Cookie values may legally contain '/' and '.' (RFC 6265 cookie-octet), so a value such as ../../<relative path> or ../../../../tmp/<file> is settable by any client, including unauthenticated ones. No other credentials or server-side artifact are required for the deletion path; Logout.jsp performs no authentication/authorization check before calling clearLoginCookie().
candidates.counterevidence_checked: jspwiki.cookieAuthentication defaults to false, which removes the login/spoofing path but not the clearLoginCookie() deletion path (verified: Logout.jsp calls the static helper unconditionally and the helper never consults allowsCookieAuthentication()). Java's File(File,String) constructor does not let an absolute child path replace the parent (child is resolved/concatenated), so traversal requires '..' segments rather than '/' prefixes; this is accounted for in the trace. getCookieFile() only proceeds when the cookie dir exists/creatable and readable/writable, which is the normal case. Privilege escalation via the login path additionally requires an exact match of the full file contents to a principal name (no trimming occurs - FileUtil.readContents(Reader) returns verbatim content), so it is conditional on file content control/knowledge. scrub() only lists the real cookie directory and does not widen the traversal.
candidates.impact: Unauthenticated, remote arbitrary file deletion with the privileges of the servlet container account (data/state destruction, e.g., work-dir serialization/state files, wiki data, configuration or logs if writable; denial of service). When cookie authentication is enabled, the same traversal converts the cookie into an authentication primitive: the contents of any readable file become the session's login principal, allowing spoofing of an existing user's login name (full impersonation of that user's page/ACL rights, potentially admin) whenever a file with matching contents exists or can be planted (e.g., uploaded attachment or page text, whose on-disk paths are derived from predictable page/attachment names). The login path also exposes arbitrary-file-derived data in the authenticated principal name shown by the UI.
candidates.prerequisites: Deletion path (default configuration): network reachability of the wiki; knowledge/guess of a target path relative to <jspwiki.workDir>/logincookies (default workDir is ${java.io.tmpdir}/JSPWiki-<appid>, so ../refmgr.ser, ../PageCount.txt, or enough ../ plus an absolute path without leading slash reach files the JVM user can delete). Login-spoofing path: jspwiki.cookieAuthentication=true (non-default), plus a readable file whose exact contents equal the target principal name; work-dir must be creatable/readable/writable by the webapp user.
candidates.root_cause: getCookieFile() composes the cookie-store path as new File(cookieDir, uid) using the raw value of the JSPWikiUID cookie, with no validation that uid is a plain UUID/non-path string and no canonicalization check that the result stays under cookieDir. HttpUtil.retrieveCookieValue() returns the cookie value verbatim (only trimming surrounding double quotes). The resolved File is then (a) opened and its exact contents used as the authenticated login principal in login(), and (b) passed to File.delete() in clearLoginCookie(). Because clearLoginCookie() is a static helper invoked unconditionally by Logout.jsp, the deletion primitive does not depend on jspwiki.cookieAuthentication being enabled.
candidates.title: Path traversal via JSPWikiUID cookie in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule (arbitrary file deletion; login-principal spoofing)
candidates.trace: Deletion: GET /Logout.jsp with Cookie: JSPWikiUID=../<target> -> Logout.jsp line 31 invokes CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.clearLoginCookie(wiki, request, response) -> clearLoginCookie line 301 getLoginCookie(request) -> HttpUtil.retrieveCookieValue() (HttpUtil.java 70-89) returns the raw value -> line 305 getCookieFile(engine, uid) -> line 213 new File(cookieDir, uid); Java resolves '..' segments -> line 309 cf.delete() removes the attacker-chosen file. Spoofing (cookie auth enabled): any request passing WikiServletFilter -> AuthenticationManager.login(request) line 300 doJAASLogin(CookieAuthenticationLoginModule) -> login() line 111 reads the same cookie, line 116 getCookieFile resolves the traversal, lines 124-125 read the file contents, line 133 adds new WikiPrincipal(fileContents, LOGIN_NAME) -> AuthenticationManager lines 304-313 mark the session AUTHENTICATED and inject roles, so authorization checks match the impersonated principal name.
candidates.unverified: Not executed or runtime-confirmed. Not verified: (1) that the deployed container accepts '../' and '/' inside a Cookie header value (RFC 6265 permits them; most parsers accept, but this was not tested in this run); (2) exact default/concrete filesystem layout on a target deployment (work-dir depth, which files exist and are writable by the JVM user); (3) whether any deployment grants the permissions/content control needed to plant a matching-content file for the spoofing variant; (4) whether servlet-container path normalization or a front proxy alters cookie values before they reach the module.
candidates.weakness_type: CWE-22 Path Traversal (secondary: CWE-287 Improper Authentication, CWE-306 Missing Authentication for Critical Function)

coverage_summary: Snapshot: 1158 model-visible files (binary look-alikes skipped by the reader). P1 index covers 1021 files / 402 Java files with 137 source files absent from the index; the index provides syntax-level symbols, calls, containment and annotation-name hints only, with control flow, data flow and semantic resolution explicitly not implemented, so indexed edges were treated as navigation hints and every candidate was re-checked against source text. I reviewed: authentication/login (AuthenticationManager, all login modules incl. CookieAuthentication and CookieAssertion, WebContainerCallbackHandler/HttpRequestCallback, SessionMonitor, WikiSession usage), authorization (AuthorizationManager, DefaultAclManager, ACL classes, PermissionFactory, permissions classes, WebContainerAuthorizer, GroupManager), user management (UserManager incl. JSONUserModule, XMLUserDatabase, JDBCUserDatabase, AbstractUserDatabase), attachment handling (AttachmentServlet, AttachmentManager, BasicAttachmentProvider, caching providers), page storage/locking/renaming (DefaultPageManager, Abstract/FileSystem/Versioning providers, PageRenamer, ReferenceManager), filters (SpamFilter, DefaultFilterManager), UI servlet layer (WikiServlet, WikiServletFilter, WikiJSPFilter, WikiRequestWrapper, CommandResolver, WikiContext, TemplateManager, Installer, InputValidator), ajax/RPC entry points (WikiAjaxDispatcherServlet, AjaxUtil, AtomAPIServlet, RPCServlet), utility code (HttpUtil, FileUtil, TextUtil, Serializer, ClassUtil), WebSocket-free front controllers, and the main JSP entry points plus both template trees (default and 210) at least at security-relevant points (Login/Logout/Edit/Comment/Delete/Group/Install/UserPreferences/Search/Rename/Wiki/PageTab/PageContent/editors, AJAXPreview/AJAXSearch/XHRHtml2Markup). No build, tests, scanners, or exploit payloads were executed.
limitations: Static, source-only review: no compilation, test execution, container deployment, or runtime confirmation was performed; nothing here is a confirmed exploit.

P1 relation index is partial (1158 source files vs 1021 indexed; 137 files missing) and supports only syntax/navigation candidates - no control-flow or data-flow proof, so reachability and taint paths are argued from manual source reading.

WEB-INF/jspwiki.policy (the default authorization policy) is not present in the snapshot, so which principals hold delete/admin/view permissions (and thus CSRF/XSS exposure for unauthenticated users) could not be verified.
Servlet-container behavior for Cookie header parsing (acceptance of '/' and '..' inside JSPWikiUID) and JSP include path normalization were not tested in this run.

I did not exhaustively review every plugin, workflow, diff provider, search provider, i18n resource, client-side JavaScript asset, or the portable Tomcat overlay; those areas are unassessed for this finding.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected/stored XSS via unescaped output of attacker-influenced values in JSP templates, e.g. templates/default/PageTab.jsp:49 <input value="${param.page}"> (rendered only for old versions), templates/default/PreferencesTab.jsp:150 ${i} (skin names, server-derived), and the <wiki:Translate>[<attachment/page name>] pattern in PageContent.jsp lines 39.
rejected_leads.reason: Plausible and individually checkable, but each requires specific render conditions or attacker-controlled values that could not be fully demonstrated statically here (page-name cleaning via MarkupParser.cleanLink strips '<'/'>'/quotes for non-existing pages; skin names come from server directories; VariableTag and c:out escape in several other spots). Weaker evidence chain than the cookie traversal for a single-candidate submission.

rejected_leads.lead: Reflected XSS through templates/default/AJAXPreview.jsp, which passes request.getParameter("wikimarkup") straight into <wiki:Translate> and returns text/html (arbitrary HTML in wiki markup is rendered verbatim).
rejected_leads.reason: Reachability/authorization depends on the view policy for the page in the request (hasAccess with WikiContext.VIEW) and on the caller template; not verified to be reachable unauthenticated in default configuration, and XSS-abuse details (victim interaction) were not established from source alone.

rejected_leads.lead: Template path traversal via the 'skin' request parameter (WikiContext.setDefaultTemplate line 821 -> setTemplate without validation -> TemplateManager.findResource builds /templates/<skin>/<name> and pageContext.include is called).
rejected_leads.reason: The include name is a fixed JSP filename appended after the attacker-controlled segment and the container normalizes include paths; no concrete arbitrary-file inclusion/execution could be confirmed from source, and impact is speculative.

rejected_leads.lead: CSRF on state-changing actions (Delete.jsp performs page/version deletion from GET parameters with no token; SpamFilter.checkHash only verifies the presence of a hidden field whose name is a global value, not its value).
rejected_leads.reason: Real design weakness but requires a privileged victim, and the default policy (jspwiki.policy is not present in the snapshot) determines who is affected; lower impact and less direct evidence than the path traversal.

rejected_leads.lead: Java deserialization of user profile attributes via Serializer.deserializeFromBase64 in XMLUserDatabase/JDBCUserDatabase.
rejected_leads.reason: No request-level write path to the serialized attribute map was found; only actors who can already write the user database can control the input.

rejected_leads.lead: AtomAPIServlet.doPost lacks authentication ('FIXME: Do authentication here') and calls WikiEngine.saveText.
rejected_leads.reason: The /atom/* servlet-mapping is commented out in the default web.xml, so the endpoint is disabled unless an administrator enables it; not the strongest reachable issue.

rejected_leads.lead: JSONUserModule /ajax/users/<uid> returns the full UserProfile (potentially including credentials) as JSON.
rejected_leads.reason: Registered with new AllPermission(null) (wildcard) in UserManager line 115, so validatePermission restricts it to administrators in the default policy model; not an authorization bypass on its own.

summary: Reviewed the Apache JSPWiki 2.11.0.M4 source snapshot (1158 model-visible files across jspwiki-main, jspwiki-war, jspwiki-util, jspwiki-portable, jspwiki-it-tests, jspwiki-wikipages). One candidate is submitted: an unvalidated path-traversal in CookieAuthenticationLoginModule.getCookieFile(), where the raw JSPWikiUID cookie value is used directly to build a File under the work-dir cookie folder. Because Logout.jsp unconditionally calls clearLoginCookie(), an unauthenticated remote request with a crafted JSPWikiUID cookie containing "../" segments reaches File.delete() on an attacker-chosen path (no authentication, no need for jspwiki.cookieAuthentication to be enabled). When jspwiki.cookieAuthentication=true the same path is also used by login(), which reads the target file's exact contents and installs them as the authenticated login principal (WikiPrincipal LOGIN_NAME), enabling identity/privilege spoofing if a file with matching contents exists or can be planted. All other plausible leads were weaker or not source-verifiable within scope and are listed as rejected leads. This is a source-evidence lead, not a runtime-confirmed exploit.
